claims.statement: Lumbini is a Buddhist pilgrimage site in what is now southern Nepal. Its archaeological remains include Ashoka’s inscribed pillar and structures dating back to the third century BCE. The pillar connects the place to a recorded royal visit, alongside the longer history of worship at the site.

Lumbini: 300 BCE to 201 BCE. Third-century BCE study window, not the lifespan of the site. UNESCO’s traditional date for the Buddha’s birth is not used here. The point is the World Heritage property reference.
